correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the strict greedy intervals J_a=(1/4+1/a,1/4+1/(a-1)] and checked all open/closed endpoint conventions. For a competing pair (x,y), x>=5; Nathanson’s necessary competitor bound 5<=x<=7<=y<4x/(x-4), proved in the cited primary paper, reduces every possible competitor for theta in I4 to 21 pairs. Independent exact Fraction enumeration (not reliance on the package log) gives 13+5+3=21 candidates, one candidate with a=11 outside the domain, and exactly 19 relevant a-values, split into 6 strictly improving and 12 tied denominators (the a=17 row has two candidates but the minimum threshold is 13/42, and a=60 has two distinct tie pairs). The exact strict-improvement thresholds and left-endpoint exclusion were checked for a=14,17,25,38,47,114; the other a-values admit no competitors by the bounding lemma. This is an infinite all-real interval proof because the analytic lemma exhausts all possible pairs before the finite count; the finite script alone would not suffice.

originality.rationale: Nathanson proves the essential general finite-competitor reduction and specializes first-denominator intervals two and three. Chu gives rational-number criteria in terms of Upsilon(p,q) and specifically the 5/16 non-greedy example belonging to a=17, but not the all-real first-denominator-four six-interval/12-tie classification. Kovač studies measure-zero eventual greediness over infinitely many terms and large first denominators; his result cannot determine the exact finite 21-candidate table. The method itself and individual failures are prior; the explicit complete next-interval partition is the candidate contribution. An unindexed equivalent special-case table remains a priority risk.
